'''Johannes F. Coy''' (born December 15, 1963, in [[Otzberg]] im [[Odenwald]]) is a German biologist and [[cancer research]]er. He is the discoverer of the genes [[TKTL1]]<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal |last1=Coy |first1=Johannes F. |last2=Dübel |first2=Stefan |last3=Kioschis |first3=Petra |last4=Thomas |first4=Karen |last5=Micklem |first5=Gos |last6=Delius |first6=Hajo |last7=Poustka |first7=Annemarie |date=1996-03-15 |title=Molecular Cloning of Tissue-Specific Transcripts of a Transketolase-Related Gene: Implications for the Evolution of New Vertebrate Genes |url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S088875439690124X |journal=Genomics |volume=32 |issue=3 |pages=309–316 |doi=10.1006/geno.1996.0124 |pmid=8838793 |issn=0888-7543|url-access=subscription }}</ref> and [[DNaseX]]<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal |last1=Coy |first1=J. F. |last2=Velhagen |first2=I. |last3=Himmele |first3=R. |last4=Delius |first4=H. |last5=Poustka |first5=A. |last6=Zentgraf |first6=H. |date=April 1996 |title=Isolation, differential splicing and protein expression of a DNase on the human X chromosome ?dopt=Abstract |journal=Cell Death and Differentiation |volume=3 |issue=2 |pages=199–206 |issn=1350-9047 |pmid=17180083}}</ref> (Apo10).<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal |last=Coy |first=Johannes F. |date=2017-04-20 |title=EDIM-TKTL1/Apo10 Blood Test: An Innate Immune System Based Liquid Biopsy for the Early Detection, Characterization and Targeted Treatment of Cancer |journal=International Journal of Molecular Sciences |volume=18 |issue=4 |page=878 |doi=10.3390/ijms18040878 |doi-access=free |issn=1422-0067 |pmc=5412459 |pmid=28425973}}</ref> According to the latest findings in evolutionary research, TKTL1 is a key gene that has triggered increased neuron formation in the [[neocortex]] and structural improvements in the brain compared to [[Neanderthal]]s, thus enabling the cognitive achievements of modern humans ([[homo sapiens]]).<ref name=":3">{{Cite journal |last1=Pinson |first1=Anneline |last2=Xing |first2=Lei |last3=Namba |first3=Takashi |last4=Kalebic |first4=Nereo |last5=Peters |first5=Jula |last6=Oegema |first6=Christina Eugster |last7=Traikov |first7=Sofia |last8=Reppe |first8=Katrin |last9=Riesenberg |first9=Stephan |last10=Maricic |first10=Tomislav |last11=Derihaci |first11=Razvan |last12=Wimberger |first12=Pauline |last13=Pääbo |first13=Svante |last14=Huttner |first14=Wieland B. |date=2022-09-09 |title=Human TKTL1 implies greater neurogenesis in frontal neocortex of modern humans than Neanderthals |url=https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/science.abl6422 |journal=Science |volume=377 |issue=6611 |article-number=eabl6422 |doi=10.1126/science.abl6422|pmid=36074851 |url-access=subscription }}</ref>

The evolutionary significance of TKTL1 was confirmed through studies by Nobel laureate [[Svante Pääbo]] and his research group at the [[Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology]]. In collaboration with [[Wieland B. Huttner]], they demonstrated that the TKTL1 gene, discovered by Johannes F. Coy, exhibits a single amino acid substitution in modern humans, leading to increased neurogenesis compared to Neanderthals.<ref name=":3" />

== Life and scientific work ==
Johannes Coy began his biology studies at the Eberhard Karls University in Tübingen in 1985, which he completed in 1990 with a focus on molecular and human genetics as well as biochemistry. In the same year, he moved to the DKFZ in Heidelberg, where he became a member of the Molecular Genome Analysis research project headed by the then DKFZ director and later [[Nobel Prize]] winner for medicine, Prof. [[Harald zur Hausen]], after completing his diploma thesis (mapping a tumor suppressor gene in neuroblastoma).

During this time, he concentrated on the identification of genes and discovered the two genes TKTL1 and DNaseX (Apo10) in this context. He was awarded summa cum laude in 1996 for his dissertation based on the discovery of these two genes. From his analyses of the TKTL1 and DNaseX (Apo10) genes, Coy concluded that both genes had the potential to be used as new diagnostic cancer markers.

In his further scientific work, Coy continued to focus on holistic research into tumor cell metabolism, in particular the use of the two genes for the early detection of cancer on the basis of diagnostic tests. He discovered that the simultaneous presence of TKTL1 and DNaseX (Apo10) in macrophages is indicative of cancer<ref name=":2" /> and contributed to the development of a blood test that makes TKTL1 and DNaseX (Apo10) detectable in macrophages.<ref name=":2"/>

He also discovered the TKTL1 [[metabolic pathway]] and the associated sugar metabolism that enables the prevention and repair of cell damage.<ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Diaz-Moralli |first1=Santiago |last2=Aguilar |first2=Esther |last3=Marin |first3=Silvia |last4=Coy |first4=Johannes F. |last5=Dewerchin |first5=Mieke |last6=Antoniewicz |first6=Maciek R. |last7=Meca-Cortés |first7=Oscar |last8=Notebaert |first8=Leen |last9=Ghesquière |first9=Bart |last10=Eelen |first10=Guy |last11=Thomson |first11=Timothy M. |last12=Carmeliet |first12=Peter |last13=Cascante |first13=Marta |date=2016-08-09 |title=A key role for transketolase-like 1 in tumor metabolic reprogramming |journal=Oncotarget |volume=7 |issue=32 |pages=51875–51897 |doi=10.18632/oncotarget.10429 |issn=1949-2553 |pmc=5239521 |pmid=27391434}}</ref><ref name=":5">{{Cite journal |last1=Langbein |first1=S. |last2=Zerilli |first2=M. |last3=Zur Hausen |first3=A. |last4=Staiger |first4=W. |last5=Rensch-Boschert |first5=K. |last6=Lukan |first6=N. |last7=Popa |first7=J. |last8=Ternullo |first8=M. P. |last9=Steidler |first9=A. |last10=Weiss |first10=C. |last11=Grobholz |first11=R. |last12=Willeke |first12=F. |last13=Alken |first13=P. |last14=Stassi |first14=G. |last15=Schubert |first15=P. |date=2006-02-27 |title=Expression of transketolase TKTL1 predicts colon and urothelial cancer patient survival: Warburg effect reinterpreted |journal=British Journal of Cancer |volume=94 |issue=4 |pages=578–585 |doi=10.1038/sj.bjc.6602962 |issn=0007-0920 |pmc=2361175 |pmid=16465194}}</ref><ref name=":6">{{Cite journal |last1=Coy |first1=Johannes F. |last2=Dressler |first2=Dirk |last3=Wilde |first3=Juergen |last4=Schubert |first4=Peter |date=2005 |title=Mutations in the transketolase-like gene TKTL1: clinical implications for neurodegenerative diseases, diabetes and cancer ?dopt=Abstract |journal=Clinical Laboratory |volume=51 |issue=5–6 |pages=257–273 |issn=1433-6510 |pmid=15991799}}</ref>

Coy's diagnostic developments as a result of his research include:

* Epitope detection in monocytes (EDIM) - detection method of biomarkers in cells of the innate immune system in blood samples
* Automated flow cytrometry method
* Flow cytometry-based blood tests

Johannes Coy holds several patents in the field of cancer research and diagnostics, including DNaseX and TKTL1:

* DNA encoding DNase and related vectors, host cells and antibodies (DNaseX)<ref>{{Cite patent|number=EP0842278B1|title=Protein mit dnase-aktivität|gdate=2005-11-09|invent1=Zentgraf|invent2=Poustka|invent3=Coy|invent4=Velhagen|inventor1-first=Hanswalter|inventor2-first=Annemarie|inventor3-first=Johannes|inventor4-first=Iris|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/EP0842278B1/de}}</ref>
* Transketolase-related protein (TKTL1)<ref>{{Cite patent|number=EP0840789B1|title=Transketolase-verwandtes protein|gdate=2006-05-31|invent1=Poustka|invent2=Coy|inventor1-first=Annemarie|inventor2-first=Johannes|url=https://patents.google.com/patent/EP0840789B1/de}}</ref>
